programme.title: Buy a castle
programme.desc: In Poland, in the early 1990s, it was possible to buy castles and palaces.However, many of these historic buildings were in very poor condition, requiring commitment, time and a lot of money.Journalist and traveler Joanna Lamparska and historian and art expert Michał Wójcik meet people whose passion is to renovate and restore neglected architectural pearls to their former glory.They travel to many places around the country, checking what efforts the new owners are making to breathe new life into historic buildings The first episode will present the story of a married couple who have been restoring the palace in Pieszyce for years.When the Hajduks took over the castle in October 2000, it was a huge ruin, with collapsed ceilings and destroyed staircases.Now, although the construction has not been completed yet, the place has regained its former splendor and splendor.The reconstruction of the palace is the largest undertaking of this type in Europe.The work has already cost over PLN 100 million.Thanks to enthusiasts such as Mr. Marian Hajduk, the palace is returning to its former glory and pleases the eyes of visitors with incredible attention to detail.

programme.title: Unobvious places
programme.desc: Katarzyna Jaroszyńska visits people who have converted buildings previously used for service or industrial purposes into houses.Marcelina and Dawid looked for their place on earth for a long time.Finally, they decided to renovate the old mushroom farm that belonged to the family.Converting a commercial building into a residential building presented many challenges.Krzysztof decided to adapt the former printing plant to his needs.He now lives in a surprising interior, from the outside resembling a cube glued to a block of flats in Wrocław.Mateusz and his relatives accidentally came across a mill during a trip to Siedlce.The view from the third floor of the building overlooking the river helped them decide to purchase this unusual building.

programme.title: Unobvious places
programme.desc: Katarzyna Jaroszyńska this time visits people whose households should be called crazy.Agnieszka is the owner of Kozi Stok, a farm located near Wieliczka, where she breeds Carpathian goats.Out of love for acrobatics and her son, the woman built a place suspended in the treetops.Jacek and his family lived in a 227-year-old wooden windmill standing in a landscape park.The renovation of this historic building became the man's true passion.Malwina inherited her love for water from her father, a sailor.The man managed to fulfill his dream of building a house on the water.It stands in Warsaw's Czerniakowski Port.

programme.title: Unobvious places
programme.desc: Katarzyna Jaroszyńska visits people who have turned ordinary allotment gardens into real gems.Alina built an arched house on her piece of land, which measures less than 14 square meters.The building is surrounded by a vegetable garden, flowerbeds and a small orchard.Aneta and her husband's plot, located near Olsztyn, is surrounded by greenery.The couple made many of its elements themselves.After Patrycja bought her own piece of land, her father and the woman's partner built a house there together.In this way, they fulfilled Patrycja's dream of having morning coffee on her own terrace.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna goes to Romania, where she visits Iana Matei, founder of the Reaching Out organization, which helps victims of human trafficking.This country is considered the European center of slavery.Iana Matei has been fighting traffickers for 18 years.He does everything he can to save the children they abuse.By stealing victims from the hands of criminals, he tries to give them back their childhood and give them a home.Her pupils call her "Mom".Iana currently cares for 15 girls.The youngest of them was sold when she was 9 years old, while another was exchanged for 4 cigarettes.During Iana's 18 years of work, she saved over 500 girls.Her biggest dream is to stop human trafficking.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna goes to Saint Petersburg, where she will meet Larisa Renar, who runs the Academy of Private Life.Women can find answers to all their questions about women's and men's issues there.Over 150,000 students have already completed courses conducted by Larisa - not only from Russia, but also from China, England, the United Arab Emirates, Bulgaria and Turkey.The heroine of the episode completed her MBA;is a psychologist, motivational trainer, and author of eight guides for women.For Russian women, whose salary is 1/3 less than men's, marriage has not only a romantic aspect, but also a business one.Hence the popularity of Larissa Academy.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska will visit Florida, where Maja Kazawiedź lives - a woman who escaped from a war-torn country - and Winter the dolphin.At Clearwater Marine Aquarium, the fates of man and animal intertwine.The heroine of the episode comes from Bosnia.She was fifteen years old when armed conflict broke out in the former Yugoslavia in 1992.Winter, in turn, as a 2-month-old baby, became entangled in the nets.Both of them came close to death, but survived thanks to their extraordinary determination and exceptional strength of character.Today they support others.Their story helped Martyna Wojciechowska in her own struggles with adversity.
